discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: strongly correlated electrons and quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that Coulomb interactions dominate the kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators realized this experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states at commensurate fillings and, upon doping, unconventional superconductivity in a pure-carbon system. This work created an entirely new, tunable platform for strong-correlation physics: with the twist angle and a gate one can sweep through Mott-like insulators, strange metals, superconductivity, orbital magnetism and quantized anomalous Hall states in a single device. Moiré materials have since become one of the most active fields in physics, including fractional Chern insulators in twisted semiconductors. The combination of a simple, elegant theoretical prediction and decisive, transformative experiments has opened a genuinely new chapter in the quantum physics of interacting electrons.
